AM13I-01.note: Borderline easy/medium: two unit-rate divisions plus a cents conversion, but all three distractors are real method errors (21.0 = the 64-oz rate itself, 6.6 = price difference over 64 oz, 17.7 = price difference over ounce difference).

AM13I-02.note: Two-step subtract-and-multiply; only 1,575 (subtracting 45 donors instead of $1,080) is a method trap, the others read as arithmetic slips.

AM13I-03.note: Single product, but the distractors are well built: 19,905.60 uses 52 weeks, 33,408 uses a 40-hour week, 17,952 drops the 40 cents.

AM13I-04.note: Two-conversion chain where each step has a direction decision; every distractor is one wrong or omitted step (6.08 stops in euros, 5.29 divides by 1.15, 1.84 skips the liter conversion).

AM13I-06.note: One proportion. 405 is the multiply-instead-of-divide trap.

AM13I-07.note: Good kind of medium-hard: the natural first approach, full perimeter x $9, lands exactly on 702, and the two partial corrections land on 675 (gate only) and 486 (building side only). Two constraints must both be carried.

AM13I-08.note: Three chained steps but no hidden setup; 8,448 punishes answering the wrong question. Some of the time here is decimal arithmetic rather than reasoning.

AM13I-09.note: The decision is the floor at the end; 45 catches stopping at total length, 8 catches dividing mass by piece length directly.

AM13I-10.note: The good kind of hard: the natural first approaches land exactly on distractors (35.0 = 15+20, 32.0 = the total decline read back as the required rise). Requires recognising that the recovery is 1/0.68, not the mirror of the fall.

AM13I-11.note: Nothing is numeric until the student sets up a ratio of ratios (1.05/1.25 x 180) with no given budget, then floors 151.2. 144 is the plain 20 percent cut, 214 inverts the two changes.

AM13I-12.note: Two-rate mixture: set up an equation that is not stated, then convert the time back to a distance for the correct leg. 121 is the other leg's distance, which is exactly where a correct solve that stops one line early lands.
